object_description: refined elongated volume with cut-outs and broken-line roof
design_condition: The building occupies the eastern half of the plot and frees the west for the playground, but its orientation and entrance turn the school’s back toward the village.

positive.statement: The volume is seductive at first glance, refined by its cut-outs and broken-line roof.

position.rationale: Distinct roof breaks and footprint cut-outs are clearly visible in the upper-right mass.

positive.statement: The typological proposal is interesting, with classrooms arranged around an elongated central hall.

position.rationale: Interior hall is approximated beneath the elongated central spine visible in the surrounding envelope.

positive.statement: The first-stage plan permits economical expansion by two or four classrooms without changing the basic typological principle or sloping roof.

position.rationale: Expansion is assigned to the elongated classroom-bearing volume, with the east side offering a plausible extension zone.

positive.statement: The prefabricated construction is economical and quick, and the materiality is convincing.

position.rationale: Material and construction claims are anchored to the complete sampled building envelope.

negative.statement: The orientation of the project, particularly the position of the entrance, is questionable because the school turns its back on the village.

position.rationale: The west edge represents the village-facing approach and likely entrance location.

negative.statement: The exterior fittings are lacking in quality, with narrow access from the village and an injudicious location of vehicles beside and within the playground.

position.rationale: West-side ground clearance approximates village access, playground, and vehicle conflict areas.

negative.statement: The hall remains the same size from one expansion stage to the next, which limits the typological proposal.

position.rationale: The hall is placed along the central elongated spine, though its interior boundary is not sampled.

negative.statement: The desired big-house appearance seems incompatible with the character of a representative building.

position.rationale: The identity judgment applies broadly to the asymmetric low-rise massing.

negative.statement: The exceptional west facade does not correspond to the floor plan, and the positioning of the windows lacks precision.

position.rationale: The west boundary of the irregular footprint provides the facade anchor.

negative.statement: The project is above average economically, with substantially more surface area and volume.

position.rationale: Cost criticism references the overall sampled volume and envelope rather than one local feature.
